claude.sample_unit: source concepts (6,179 medication names and 2,261 laboratory test names)

links.outcome: Top-1 accuracy for lab test mapping before vs after fine-tuning on local data
links.effect: BioLORD top-1 accuracy rose from 37.0% (baseline) to 91.6% after fine-tuning on local hospital data; all models reached 89.0-93.0% top-1 with full training data.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate the importance of domain-specific fine-tuning, with top-1 accuracy for laboratory test names increasing from 37.0% to 91.6%.

links.outcome: Mapping accuracy on a held-out new hospital and variation across hospitals
links.effect: Weighted top-1 accuracy on an unseen hospital was 73.5% vs 91.6% fully fine-tuned; per-hospital finetuned top-1 ranged 25.0% to 96.3%; baseline std across hospitals 7.9% for lab tests.
links.quote: However, when simulating the onboarding of a new hospital, the system achieves a weighted average top-1 accuracy of only 73.5%, indicating substantial variability across NHS hospital systems.

links.outcome: Real-world lab test mapping accuracy vs published benchmark performance
links.effect: Models reporting 80%-90% top-1 on standard benchmarks achieved baseline top-1 below 40% on real NHS laboratory test names (BioLORD 37.0%).
links.quote: Consequently, baseline top-1 accuracies remain below 40%, underscoring that pre-training on biomedical literature and ontology definitions alone is insufficient to capture the extreme variability and abbreviation patterns encountered in laboratory test naming.

links.outcome: Cosine similarity confidence for correct vs incorrect predictions
links.effect: Mean cosine similarity 0.97 ± 0.06 for correct (n=457) vs 0.81 ± 0.14 for incorrect (n=64) predictions; Welch t=8.8, p<0.01.
links.quote: Results indicate a significant difference in mean similarity score under Welch's t -test (t-statistic: 8.8 p -value <0.01), highlighting the model's ability to quantify uncertainty in its predictions.

unlisted_practices: Continuous learning pipeline that retrains the model on expert-validated mappings (top-1 on hold-out rose 89.43% to 94.22%, p=0.021)
Human-in-the-loop review interface presenting top-5 suggestions for expert validation vs manual spreadsheet mapping (>2-fold efficiency gain)
Restricting edit permissions to trained users with read-only access for downstream consumers to limit error propagation into model updates

openai.sample_unit: source concepts mapped or marked not relevant in 10 real-world ArcMAP sessions by one clinical informatician

links.outcome: Laboratory concept mapping accuracy after local fine-tuning
links.effect: BioLORD laboratory-test top-1 accuracy increased from 37.0% without fine-tuning to 91.6% after domain-specific fine-tuning.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate the importance of domain-specific fine-tuning, with top-1 accuracy for laboratory test names increasing from 37.0% to 91.6%.

links.outcome: Mapping accuracy when generalizing to an unseen hospital
links.effect: BioLORD top-1 accuracy decreased from 91.6% in the fully fine-tuned setting to 73.5% when evaluated on hospitals excluded from training.
links.quote: Evaluating the onboarding of a new hospital (Exp1-S3) revealed a reduction in mean performance, with BioLORD's top-1 accuracy decreasing from 91.6% in the fully fine-tuned setting to 73.5%.

links.outcome: Real-world session accuracy compared with static hold-out performance
links.effect: Static hold-out top-1 accuracy increased from 89.43% to 94.22%; real-world session accuracy ranged from 80.26% to 98.15%, with an additional low outlier of 56.7% in session 2.
links.quote: In contrast, top-1 accuracy on session-specific test sets exhibited greater variability, ranging from 80.26% to 98.15%, with one notable outlier in session 2 ( acc top1 = 56.7%).

links.effect: estimated >2-fold increase in efficiency when using ArcMAP compared to manual sessions
links.quote: In contrast, during the manual mapping sessions without ArcMAP, only 31.7 ± 0.9 ( Supplementary Table 2 ) concepts were mapped on average, resulting in an estimated >2-fold increase in efficiency when using ArcMAP.

links.effect: achieved a weighted average top-1 accuracy of only 73.5% across new hospital systems
links.quote: However, when simulating the onboarding of a new hospital, the system achieves a weighted average top-1 accuracy of only 73.5%, indicating substantial variability across NHS hospital systems.

links.outcome: top-1 accuracy for laboratory test names
links.effect: increased from 37.0% to 91.6% after domain-specific fine-tuning
links.quote: Our results demonstrate the importance of domain-specific fine-tuning, with top-1 accuracy for laboratory test names increasing from 37.0% to 91.6%.

links.effect: significant difference in mean similarity score between correct (0.97) and incorrect (0.81) predictions
links.quote: Results indicate a significant difference in mean similarity score under Welch's t-test (t-statistic: 8.8 p-value <0.01), highlighting the model's ability to quantify uncertainty in its predictions.

unlisted_practices: Continuous active learning during production mapping sessions to incrementally update embeddings based on user-validated mappings

screen.practice: human-in-the-loop expert review with continuous fine-tuning
screen.reason: Evaluates a real-world deployed human-in-the-loop EHR concept mapping tool across five NHS hospitals, specifically testing the impact of a continuous learning/fine-tuning pipeline from clinician feedback.
